companion.npm_status: aqua-companion is also published on npm. aqua-mcp-server on npm includes it and is the primary install, so use that; the tarball above is the fallback.

mcp_server.status: aqua-mcp-server is published on npm and is the primary install: `npx -y aqua-mcp-server`. It includes the companion and serves the same tools. Versions below 2.0 are legacy and must not be used.

hosted_mcp.transport: Streamable HTTP (POST JSON-RPC, JSON responses, stateless; no SSE stream)
hosted_mcp.scope: read-only public catalog tools, resources and prompts; no authentication, no workspace tools; rate-limited
hosted_mcp.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http aqua-public https://aquaidp.xyz/mcp

catalog_config.rule: use the publishable/anon key only; they refuse any other role and fetch the configuration only from https://aquaidp.xyz (or a local override file)
catalog_config.auto_refresh: discover_applications, get_application_details and match_canonical_questions refresh an empty or stale cache (older than 24 hours; AQUA_CATALOG_MAX_AGE_HOURS changes it, 0 turns it off) with the same public read-only request as refresh_catalog. Offline or unconfigured, they answer from the cache and return catalog_empty: run refresh_catalog when there is nothing cached

install.mcp_claude_code: claude mcp add aqua -- npx -y aqua-mcp-server --keychain
install.mcp_claude_code_with_workspace: claude mcp add aqua -- npx -y aqua-mcp-server --workspace <folder>/AQUA --keychain
install.mcp_companion_cli: npx -y aqua-mcp-server companion <command>   # for example: companion init --path <folder>, companion doctor, companion export-backup <file> --workspace <folder>/AQUA
install.claude_code: claude mcp add aqua -- npx --yes https://aquaidp.xyz/companion/aqua-companion-0.2.5.tgz mcp --keychain
install.claude_code_with_workspace: claude mcp add aqua -- npx --yes https://aquaidp.xyz/companion/aqua-companion-0.2.5.tgz mcp --workspace <folder>/AQUA --keychain

tiers.meaning: Always allowed. Only reads the workspace or the public catalog cache.
Stages private records in the user's local workspace (drafts, imports, evidence). Refused in --read-only mode. Never approves anything.
Acts only after the human confirms in the MCP client UI (elicitation). Without that capability it returns requires_human with the exact command for the user to run.
Never acts. Returns requires_human with the steps the user takes in the AQUA browser app (approve, sign, freeze/export, submit, attest).

tools.name: add_question
tools.title: add_question
tools.summary: Manually index one question in an application with its exact source wording — for fields the extractor missed or fields added after a later capture.

tools.name: approve_answer
tools.title: approve_answer
tools.summary: Never executes.

tools.name: assemble_application
tools.title: assemble_application
tools.summary: Build a Markdown application from explicitly chosen APPROVED answer versions plus the unresolved fields and provenance.

tools.name: attach_evidence
tools.title: attach_evidence
tools.summary: Stage an evidence record for a file the user placed in inbox/ (its sha256 is recorded) and optionally link it to a version.

tools.name: attest_submission
tools.title: attest_submission
tools.summary: Never executes.

tools.name: create_draft_version
tools.title: create_draft_version
tools.summary: Stage a NEW, unapproved draft version of an answer in this workspace (method recorded as an agent draft).

tools.name: discover_applications
tools.title: discover_applications
tools.summary: Search the cached public AQUA catalog (approved programs) and list the applications in this workspace.

tools.name: doctor
tools.title: doctor
tools.summary: Self-check: Node and companion version, the public catalog configuration (source, origin, key role: only anon/publishable is accepted), connectivity and a canonical-only catalog read (counts only), workspace and macOS…

tools.name: export_packet
tools.title: export_packet
tools.summary: Never executes.

tools.name: get_application_details
tools.title: get_application_details
tools.summary: Full template of one application: exact question wording, parsed requirements (limits, required, time context, qualifiers), deadline and time zone, and where the data came from and how it was verified.

tools.name: hub_find_similar_questions
tools.title: hub_find_similar_questions
tools.summary: Find canonical questions in the approved catalog that ask about the same thing as the given text (lexical similarity over question wording and its recorded variants; no embeddings, nothing stored).

tools.name: hub_get_acceptance_stats
tools.title: hub_get_acceptance_stats
tools.summary: Public acceptance figures for one approved canonical program: acceptance rate and application count where public, and counts of verified applicant-reported outcomes by cohort (counts only, never who reported).

tools.name: hub_get_heat_scores
tools.title: hub_get_heat_scores
tools.summary: Approved canonical programs ranked by heat score (current applicant interest and deadline pressure).

tools.name: hub_get_program_by_slug
tools.title: hub_get_program_by_slug
tools.summary: One approved canonical program by slug with its public stats and theme weights (DNA) in a single call.

tools.name: hub_get_program_detail
tools.title: hub_get_program_detail
tools.summary: Full public detail for one approved canonical program by program_id or slug: deadlines, cycles, rolling/cohort, value and acceptance figures where public.

tools.name: hub_get_program_dna
tools.title: hub_get_program_dna
tools.summary: Theme weight breakdown of one approved canonical program (what it emphasizes, from its questions), by program_id or slug.

tools.name: hub_get_program_questions
tools.title: hub_get_program_questions
tools.summary: The application questions of one approved canonical program in display order: exact wording (in untrusted_content), word and character limits, required flag, theme, and how many approved programs ask the same canonica…

tools.name: hub_get_program_rankings
tools.title: hub_get_program_rankings
tools.summary: Approved canonical programs ranked by program value score (what you get versus what you give up, relative to application effort).

tools.name: hub_get_question_significance
tools.title: hub_get_question_significance
tools.summary: How much one canonical question matters across approved programs: how many ask it and what share of approved programs that is, typical limits, theme, and which programs ask it.

tools.name: hub_get_universal_questions
tools.title: hub_get_universal_questions
tools.summary: Canonical questions asked by most approved programs: the ones to answer first.

tools.name: hub_search_programs
tools.title: hub_search_programs
tools.summary: Search approved canonical AQUA programs (accelerators, grants, fellowships, VC and other programs) by words, type, status, equity, cash, rolling and deadline window.

tools.name: import_history
tools.title: import_history
tools.summary: Batch-stage applications the user ALREADY SUBMITTED (a folder inside the workspace inbox/, .md .txt .docx .html .json .csv) as history records: exact question wording, the submitted answer, program, source file sha256…

tools.name: import_local_application
tools.title: import_local_application
tools.summary: Stage a private local application from a file the user placed in the workspace inbox/ folder (.txt, .md, .html, .csv, .json, .docx).

tools.name: init_workspace
tools.title: init_workspace
tools.summary: Create an encrypted AQUA workspace ONLY after the user confirms the folder and consent in the MCP client UI (elicitation).

tools.name: inspect_extracted_questions
tools.title: inspect_extracted_questions
tools.summary: Show how the questions of a workspace application were extracted: exact wording, parsed requirements, source location, and items the parser was unsure about.

tools.name: link_answer
tools.title: link_answer
tools.summary: Mark an approved answer version as a direct-reuse candidate for a later question.

tools.name: link_history
tools.title: link_history
tools.summary: Record a relevance link between an imported history answer (a submitted, unconfirmed record) and a workspace question.

tools.name: locate_workspace
tools.title: locate_workspace
tools.summary: Where the AQUA workspace is (or would be created): whether this server has one open, the configured path, the folders searched, and the exact init command.

tools.name: mark_question
tools.title: mark_question
tools.summary: Mark a question not_applicable (hidden by an observed branch), skipped (known optional field deliberately left blank), or clear it back to open — always with a reason.

tools.name: match_canonical_questions
tools.title: match_canonical_questions
tools.summary: Match an application's questions (or given question texts) against canonical questions in the cached public catalog with the tiered matcher (exact, normalized, semantic, novel).

tools.name: prepare_catalog_candidate
tools.title: prepare_catalog_candidate
tools.summary: Build a sanitized public catalog candidate (program, deadlines, public question wording only) from a staged application imported with a public source_url.

tools.name: prepare_packet
tools.title: prepare_packet
tools.summary: Readiness report for freezing an application packet: per question the selectable approved version, whether its approval is bound to the exact hash, length limits, required questions, and content integrity.

tools.name: present_review_decisions
tools.title: present_review_decisions
tools.summary: Build the offline AQUA review file (HTML, containing the user's answers in plain text) for one application and save it under exports/reviews/ (at most 25 files are kept; refused under --read-only).

tools.name: read_review_status
tools.title: read_review_status
tools.summary: Derived review status of every question in an application (gap, suggested, needs evidence, under review, approved, ...) and the Direct / Adapt / Gap reuse recommendation against the rest of the answer bank.

tools.name: record_observed_submission
tools.title: record_observed_submission
tools.summary: Store an observation that an application may have been submitted (for example a confirmation e-mail the user saved in inbox/), flagged requires_human_attestation.

tools.name: refresh_catalog
tools.title: refresh_catalog
tools.summary: Fetch approved canonical programs, cycles and questions from the configured public AQUA catalog endpoint (read-only, public key, nothing from the workspace is sent).

tools.name: request_evidence
tools.title: request_evidence
tools.summary: Record an evidence gap on a version (what support is missing).

tools.name: search_answer_bank
tools.title: search_answer_bank
tools.summary: Search the user's private answers, versions, facts and evidence in this workspace (decrypted in memory only).

tools.name: sign_packet
tools.title: sign_packet
tools.summary: Never executes.

tools.name: submit_catalog_candidate
tools.title: submit_catalog_candidate
tools.summary: Never executes.

tools.name: sync_from_vault_export
tools.title: sync_from_vault_export
tools.summary: Import an encrypted backup the user exported from the AQUA browser vault and placed in the workspace inbox/ (the same checks as "aqua-companion import-backup": integrity, account binding, conflicts recorded, nothing o…

tools.name: update_question
tools.title: update_question
tools.summary: Add interpretation or correct metadata on a question — summary, general/custom kind, topic, group, required status, limit, visible options — without ever changing the captured source wording.

tools.name: verify_packet
tools.title: verify_packet
tools.summary: Verify an exported AQUA packet JSON placed in inbox/ (or packets/): canonical manifest, manifest hash, packet id, per-answer hashes, provenance receipts and the signature if present.

intentionally_absent.name: publish_catalog_entry
intentionally_absent.why: Catalog publication needs reviewer authorization and source verification in the AQUA service; the agent can only prepare a candidate.

intentionally_absent.name: run_migration
intentionally_absent.why: Database migrations change production permissions and require explicit owner authorization.

intentionally_absent.name: admin_platform
intentionally_absent.why: Platform administration (users, roles, billing, teams) is not a user capability.

intentionally_absent.name: configure_security
intentionally_absent.why: Security configuration (RLS, keys, service-role access) is owner-only and never handled by agents.

intentionally_absent.name: read_hosted_answers
intentionally_absent.why: Private answers live in the browser vault and this workspace; the agent never gets database or service-role access.

intentionally_absent.name: TRANSPORT=http (self-hosted HTTP)
intentionally_absent.why: 1.x served unauthenticated write-capable HTTP. 2.0 has stdio locally and the read-only hosted endpoint only.

journey.how: npx -y aqua-mcp-server --help (primary, from npm). Fallback: the companion tarball, npx --yes https://aquaidp.xyz/companion/aqua-companion-0.2.5.tgz --help (check the published sha256 first; for a downloaded copy use npx --yes --package <path>.tgz aqua-companion)

init_workspace (the user confirms the folder in the MCP client) or the user runs `aqua-companion init --path <folder>`, which creates <folder>/AQUA; then restart the MCP server with --workspace <folder>/AQUA. The passphrase is typed by the user, never sent through the model

the user copies past submitted applications into a folder inside the workspace inbox/ (for example inbox/history/); import_history { folder: "history" } stages them; the user exports a backup and confirms them at https://aquaidp.xyz/history
import_local_application (a file in inbox/) or get_application_details for a catalog program
create_draft_version stages unapproved drafts; request_evidence / attach_evidence
the user runs export-backup <file> --workspace <folder>/AQUA, restores it at https://aquaidp.xyz/aqua-local and approves each answer on the browser review board
the user exports a browser backup into inbox/; sync_from_vault_export imports it; read_review_status shows approved with the hash preserved
prepare_packet (readiness), the user freezes/exports in the browser, verify_packet checks the export. Nothing is ever submitted by the agent.
